evidence.excerpt: This book chapter documents the practical process of developing boundary-scan test programmes for engine control units that must comply with ISO 26262 ASIL-B requirements. It covers the workflow from netlist import through BSDL file validation, cluster-based test step generation, and diagnostic coverage estimation. Particular attention is given to conflicts between scan-clock frequency requirements and EMC constraints on automotive boards, and to the documentation artefacts required for functional safety audits. The chapter draws on experience from three development cycles carried out in collaboration with a regional electronics manufacturer over four years. Quantitative data are provided on coverage achieved, defect escapes observed during pilot production, and rework costs attributed to test-strategy decisions. The chapter concludes with a checklist of 22 items for teams beginning boundary-scan development on safety-relevant ECUs.
